text:
Winnipeg traded Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey in late October, the end of an era for a franchise that built itself around him. On Tuesday the Devils kept him out of the game in Winnipeg, Kyle Connor said he was surprised, and the Jets won anyway, 4-2, behind two goals from Dawson Mercer and 19 saves from Nico Daws, two of the players they got back. It was their fourth straight win.

The streak looks earned: 19-11 in goals and 62% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those four games. It includes a historic comeback sparked by Tyrel Bauer's Gordie Howe hat trick and a last-second power-play winner from Mark Scheifele against Tampa Bay.

The season is more modest. At 8-8-3 the Jets get 48% of the chances, have allowed 65 goals in 19 games, and sit at 22% to make the playoffs in our simulations. Life without an elite goalie means the team in front has to be better than it has been for most of the year. The Scheifele, Connor and Cole Perfetti line is the engine, but it gives up nearly as much as it creates.

The front office has already made a hard call on youth, waiving Brad Lambert and sending him to Manitoba. What to watch: whether this run is the start of a new identity or a hot week. If the Jets keep winning the chance battle like this, the odds will move quickly.
headline: The Jets found life after Hellebuyck
